back: Extracting or growing raw materials: farming, mining, quarrying, forestry and fishing.
Manufacturing and processing raw materials or parts into finished goods; construction is usually included.
Providing services to people and businesses, such as retail, transport, banking, health, education and tourism.
Knowledge-based services: research and development, ICT, consultancy and specialist information processing.
The percentage of a country's workers employed in each sector of industry.

front: Typical employment structure of an LIC
back: Most workers in primary industry (mainly farming by hand); small secondary and tertiary sectors.

front: Typical employment structure of an HIC
back: Very few primary workers (mechanised), a shrinking secondary sector, and most workers in tertiary and quaternary jobs.
As a country develops: primary employment falls, secondary rises then falls, tertiary rises throughout.
The decline of manufacturing employment in a country, through automation and factories moving abroad.
Primary (minerals, tobacco) earns most foreign currency; secondary adds value and creates urban jobs; tertiary (tourism, transport, banking) supports the economy.
